title: Impact of Nonlinearities on Local Kinetic and Thermokinetic Uncertainty Relations in Bosonic Transport
authors: Didrik Palmqvist, Luca Magazzù, Milena Grifoni, Janine Splettstoesser
abstract: The precision of transport observables can be bounded by the entropy production and the activity of the transport process via kinetic and thermokinetic uncertainty relations. In linear bosonic systems, such uncertainty relations can provide tight bounds when the activity is replaced by a local activity of the measurement contact of interest---even in the strong-coupling regime. How much nonlinearities (or interactions) impact the validity and predictiveness of these local bounds and how much this impact depends on the concrete definition of activity are open questions that we address for two experimentally relevant model systems, a harmonic oscillator network and the intrinsically nonlinear spin-boson model. We thereby provide experimentally testable predictions on how nonlinearities impact or even break local kinetic and thermokinetic precision bounds.
summary: This paper theoretically examines how interactions and nonlinearities impact fundamental uncertainty relations that bound the precision of measurements in bosonic quantum transport. By analyzing model systems like the spin-boson model, the authors show that while local bounds are tight for linear systems, nonlinearity can significantly alter or invalidate these established predictive limits.
main_problem: The study investigates how nonlinearities (interactions) affect the validity and predictive power of local kinetic and thermokinetic uncertainty relations governing bosonic transport.
main_result: The paper demonstrates that while linear systems allow for tight, locally defined precision bounds, these bounds are impacted or potentially broken when strong nonlinear interactions are present in the steady-state regime.
method: The analysis employs theoretical tools including the Gorini–Kossakowski–Sudarshan–Lindblad (GKSL) master equation, Full Counting Statistics (FCS), and derivations of various activity measures to establish bounds.
model_or_system: The work analyzes bosonic transport in two specific models: a harmonic oscillator network and the intrinsically nonlinear spin-boson model (NESB). The general framework involves an open quantum system coupled to Markovian baths.
key_observables: Precision $P(X) := (I(X))^2 / S(X)$, entropy production ($\sigma$), local/global activity measures, and current noise ($S(N)$).
important_parameters: The analysis focuses on the transition from linear to nonlinear regimes, and the dependence of bounds on the specific definition of 'activity'.
main_assumptions: Approximations used include Born, Markov, and secular approximations when deriving correlator-based activity definitions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 sketches illustrate the physical setups: a harmonic oscillator network coupled to two reservoirs, the single oscillator limit, and the NESB model under strong nonlinearities.
paper_structure: The paper first reviews the theoretical framework of uncertainty relations in bosonic transport. It then develops multiple definitions for dynamical activity using Green's functions and correlators, showing their mathematical equivalence under approximations. Finally, it applies these tools to analyze how nonlinearity affects the derived local precision bounds in specific model systems.
why_interesting: This is highly relevant as it bridges non-equilibrium thermodynamics (entropy production) with quantum transport theory, providing concrete predictions about measurement limitations in interacting nanoscale devices.
